questions.stem: Which type of DNA replication was proposed by Watson and Crick?
choices: Conservative replication
Semi-conservative replication
Dispersive replication
Full replication
questions.solution: Watson and Crick proposed that DNA replication is semi-conservative, meaning each new DNA molecule contains one original strand and one newly synthesized strand. Conservative replication would keep the original DNA strands together, which contradicts the structure they proposed. Dispersive replication suggests the DNA is fragmented and reassembled, which is not supported by their model. Full replication is not a recognized type of DNA replication in this context.

questions.stem: What was the result of the DNA extracted from the culture one generation after the transfer from N to N medium?
choices: It had light density DNA only
It had heavy density DNA only
It had hybrid or intermediate density DNA
It had a mix of heavy and light DNA
questions.solution: The DNA extracted one generation after the transfer had a hybrid or intermediate density because it contained both original and newly synthesized strands. Light density DNA only would imply no new DNA was made, which is incorrect. Heavy density DNA only would suggest no dilution of the original DNA, which also doesn't match the results. A mix of heavy and light DNA would not occur because the replication process forms hybrids.

questions.critique: The question refers to the classic Meselson-Stahl experiment, where DNA was labeled with heavy nitrogen (15N) and then transferred to light nitrogen (14N) medium. After one generation, the DNA was found to be hybrid (15N-14N), not purely light or heavy. The reasoning in the author's solution is accurate and matches the expected understanding of semi-conservative replication.

questions.stem: What is the role of DNA-dependent DNA polymerase in DNA replication?
choices: To break the DNA strands
To add new nucleotides to a growing DNA strand
To separate the DNA strands
To provide energy for the replication process
questions.solution: DNA-dependent DNA polymerase adds new nucleotides to a growing DNA strand by using an existing DNA strand as a template. This process ensures accurate replication of the genetic material. Helicase is responsible for breaking and separating the DNA strands, while deoxyribonucleoside triphosphates provide the energy needed for the reaction.

questions.stem: Why is DNA considered more stable than RNA as a genetic material?
choices: DNA has a 2-OH group at each nucleotide
RNA is double-stranded, whereas DNA is single-stranded
DNA has thymine, whereas RNA has uracil
DNA is not reactive and is less prone to degradation
questions.solution: DNA is considered more stable than RNA because it is less reactive and less prone to degradation. The 2-OH group in RNA makes it labile and easily degradable, while DNA lacks this group. DNA is not single-stranded, and RNA does not have thymine; it has uracil. The presence of thymine in DNA also adds stability, but the main reason is the lack of the reactive 2-OH group in DNA.

mr.stem: DNA लहान जीनेटिक पदार्थ म्हणून रीतसर निश्चित केला जातो कारण काय?

questions.stem: If a DNA molecule has a sequence of bases on one strand, what can be said about the sequence on the other strand?
choices: It is completely random and unrelated
It is identical to the first strand
It is complementary to the first strand
It is the reverse of the first strand
questions.solution: The sequence on the other DNA strand is complementary because each base pairs specifically with its complement—adenine with thymine and cytosine with guanine. This ensures that the two strands are not random, identical, or reversed, but rather mirror each other in a specific way. The correct option reflects the fundamental principle of DNA structure.

questions.stem: Which of the following best describes the role of histones in the packaging of DNA in eukaryotic cells?
choices: They provide a rigid framework for DNA to attach to
They help in the replication of DNA
They neutralize the negative charge of DNA
They prevent DNA from being transcribed
questions.solution: Histones are positively charged proteins that bind to the negatively charged DNA, helping to package it into a compact structure. This neutralization of charge allows DNA to be organized into nucleosomes and further into chromatin. The other options are incorrect because histones do not provide a rigid framework, they are not directly involved in DNA replication, and they do not prevent transcription.

questions.stem: What did the Hershey-Chase experiment demonstrate about the role of DNA in viral infection?
choices: DNA is the only genetic material in viruses
Proteins are the primary genetic material
DNA is the material that enters the bacterial cell during infection
RNA is the only genetic material in viruses
questions.solution: The Hershey-Chase experiment demonstrated that DNA is the material that enters the bacterial cell during infection. This was shown by using radioactive labeling and separating the viral coats from the bacteria. The experiment ruled out proteins as the genetic material and showed that DNA is the key to viral replication. RNA is not the only genetic material, and DNA is clearly involved in viral replication.

questions.stem: A scientist found that a virus's genetic material can be both DNA and RNA. Which of the following is most likely true about this virus?
